chapter: Learning from players; Jonah Jones lessons
title: Eddie Barefield and Willow Weep for Me
summary: Maxwell sat in with Eddie Barefield's band in 1938 and still admires him.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Bix Beiderbecke: hearing, copying and remembering him

blocks.x: Yeah, I have that record. And I have a great record of Calloway's called 'Willow Weep for me.' And I always thought that was Eddie Barefield and somebody --
No, on tenor sax. No, Hilton Jefferson, oh, yes.

Yeah, that's what somebody told me. All these years I'd keep talking to Eddie Barefield about how great he played on that, and he's never cracked. Because I've known Eddie Barefield since 1938, he had a band out in the Cotton Club, 80 pieces. And he used to let me come out and sit in with his band. And then later he came to New York and I played in Nick's with his band. But I was just a kid then. And he used to write these arrangements in five and six sharps, goddamn this keys. But he has always been nice to me, all my life.
Same with me, one of my teachers.
He's one of my best friends.
